cards.title: Introduction to Routing
cards.content:
Routing in ASP.NET Core is responsible for matching incoming HTTP requests and dispatching them to the app's executable endpoints, such as controllers or Minimal APIs.

Routing is typically configured in Program.cs using middleware.

options.text: To connect to the database and execute queries.
To match incoming HTTP requests to executable endpoints.
To serialize objects into JSON format.
To handle user authentication and authorization only.

cards.title: Convention-based vs Attribute Routing
cards.content:
ASP.NET Core supports two primary types of routing:

  • Convention-based routing: Defines global routing patterns that apply to all controllers in the application. Commonly used for traditional MVC apps (e.g., {controller=Home}/{action=Index}/{id?}).
  • Attribute routing: Uses attributes (like [HttpGet("products/{id}")]) on controllers and action methods to define routes directly. Highly recommended for REST APIs.

content.text: To add routing services to the Dependency Injection container in Program.cs, we typically call builder.Services.AddControllers(); which includes routing, but to configure the middleware pipeline we must call app.Use______(); before MapControllers().

cards.title: Route Parameters and Constraints
cards.content:
Route parameters are captured using curly braces {id}. You can also apply inline constraints to validate parameter types.

[HttpGet("users/{id:int}")]
public IActionResult GetUser(int id)
{
    return Ok();
}

Common constraints include int, bool, guid, minlength, and alpha.

pairs.right: Ensures the parameter is a valid integer
Ensures the string length is exactly 5
Ensures the parameter parses as a DateTime
Ensures the string contains only alphabetic characters

cards.title: Routing Best Practices
cards.content:
Key takeaways for ASP.NET Core Routing:

  • Prefer Attribute Routing for RESTful APIs to keep route definitions close to actions.
  • Use Route Constraints to enforce types and prevent unnecessary model validation failures.
  • Ensure correct middleware order in Program.cs: Routing must execute before Authorization and Endpoint mapping.
